section_summary: This section records Japanese rules for foreign aircraft and U.S. efforts to publish accurate guidance for American aviators. It includes a 1936 amendment to Japan’s Aviation Law, a later correction establishing that foreign commercial flights could still operate with administrative approval, and full Embassy translations of the law and amendment. File notes and cross-references cover flights near Rota, Japanese aviation policy, tariffs, and a proposed Nagoya airport.

subfiles.title: Note verbale on foreign aviators and Japanese regulations
subfiles.about: Requests advance diplomatic inquiries by American aviators and warns of flight suspensions for regulatory violations.
subfiles.summary: Japan asks the Embassy to help aviators obtain entry conditions and says offending foreign aviators will face the same flight restrictions as Japanese aviators.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs routing note
subfiles.about: Suggests forwarding Commerce-related aviation information to the Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten routing suggestion concerning copies for the Embassy; OCR obscures details.

subfiles.title: Treaty Division note on aviation pamphlet
subfiles.about: Discusses publication of Japanese aviation information in a broader foreign-country pamphlet.
subfiles.summary: Notes the pamphlet is unfinished and Japanese information may first appear in the Air Commerce Bulletin.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Ambassador Forbes on aviator warnings
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports proposed additions to published advice for American aviators flying to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department proposes warning that violators may lose Japanese flight privileges and that aviators should consult the Embassy about admission conditions.

subfiles.title: Letter to Commerce on revised Japan flight guidance
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Proposes adding Japanese enforcement and advance-inquiry warnings to public aviation guidance.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Japanese note and asks Commerce to add two paragraphs explaining suspension of violators’ flights and the need to obtain Embassy advice before flying to Japan.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of revised guidance
subfiles.about: Confirms publication of the additional Japan guidance.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will include the information in the December 15 Air Commerce Bulletin.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of instructions on Asian air navigation summaries
subfiles.about: Sends instructions to missions in Japan, China, and Siam to keep aviation summaries current.
subfiles.summary: State sends Commerce copies of instructions requesting updated air navigation requirements.

subfiles.title: Treaty Division note on draft instructions
subfiles.about: Explains that draft instructions for China, Japan, and Siam match earlier update requests.
subfiles.summary: The drafts correspond to requests previously prepared for Latin American missions and Paris.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Ambassador Grew to update Japan aviation summary
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests periodic checks for material changes in Japanese air navigation law.
subfiles.summary: Grew is asked to consult Japanese authorities as appropriate and submit a complete replacement summary if the published guidance needs revision.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of March 24 instructions
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of instructions on keeping Asian aviation summaries current.
subfiles.summary: Commerce thanks State for copies of the instructions.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Japan’s air navigation requirements
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese confirmation that the published Japan summary remains accurate.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities reviewed page 306 of the Air Commerce Bulletin and found no revision necessary.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Grew’s confirmation to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards confirmation that the published Japanese aviation data remains current.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Grew’s May 12 despatch for the Aeronautics Branch.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of Grew’s despatch
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the confirmation that published Japanese aviation requirements remain accurate.
subfiles.summary: Commerce thanks State for the information.

subfiles.title: Yokohama driver’s-license file note
subfiles.about: Points to a separate file on Japan’s demanding automobile driver examination.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to file 164.21.

subfiles.title: Yokohama General Motors–Nissan file note
subfiles.about: Points to a separate file on a proposed General Motors–Nissan merger.
subfiles.summary: Notes a newspaper report that merger talks failed.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Japan’s 1936 commercial aviation amendment
subfiles.about: Reports an amendment concerning foreign commercial flights to and from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reads the amendment as barring foreign paid passenger or cargo service between Japan and abroad, and discusses possible effects on international aviation.

subfiles.title: Translation of Law No. 34 of 1936
subfiles.about: Translates amendments to Japan’s Aviation Law.
subfiles.summary: The amendments define aircraft and aviation, regulate obstacles near aerodromes, revise compensation rules, address beacons, and extend Article 35 to transport between Japan and points abroad.

subfiles.title: Commerce correction of Embassy interpretation
subfiles.about: Corrects the interpretation of Japan’s amended Article 35.
subfiles.summary: After consulting the Japanese Embassy’s official text, Commerce finds that the amendment only inserts additional route language. The existing clause allowing flights with administrative approval remains in force.

subfiles.title: Southgate acknowledgment of corrected law
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the significance of the retained approval clause.
subfiles.summary: Southgate says he will relay the correction to the Embassy.

subfiles.title: Instruction requesting complete translation
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests a complete translation of Japan’s Aviation Law after the Article 35 correction.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Embassy to verify and translate the law in full.

subfiles.title: Grew’s despatch enclosing full aviation-law translation
subfiles.about: Submits Embassy translations of the 1921 Aviation Law and its 1936 amendment.
subfiles.summary: Encloses translations from Teikoku Hoki.

subfiles.title: Translation of Japan’s Aviation Law, Law No. 54
subfiles.about: Provides the complete translated text of Japan’s original Aviation Law.
subfiles.summary: The law defines Japanese aircraft and establishes rules for inspection, registration, crew licensing, airfields, routes, foreign aircraft, commercial transport, customs, quarantine, and enforcement. Article 35 permits foreign aircraft to carry paying passengers or goods between Japanese points only with administrative permission. Its later chapters set penalties for safety offenses and regulatory violations.

subfiles.title: Translation of 1936 amendment to the Aviation Law
subfiles.about: Provides the complete translated text of Law No. 34 amending Japan’s Aviation Law.
subfiles.summary: The amendment updates aircraft definitions, licensing, aerodrome safety zones, and beacon rules. It adds routes between Japan and points abroad to Article 35 while leaving the original permission clause intact.

subfiles.title: Pan American Airways flight near Rota file note
subfiles.about: Points to a letter disputing an alleged unauthorized flight over Rota.
subfiles.summary: Says Captain Musick’s aircraft passed north of Rota en route from Midway to Guam.

subfiles.title: Unknown aircraft over Rota file note
subfiles.about: Points to a report of a possible Pan American Airways flight over Rota.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities request a warning against another overflight.

subfiles.title: National policy aviation company cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on a new national policy aviation company.
subfiles.summary: Original despatch encloses translations of company legislation.

subfiles.title: Commercial aviation tariffs cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to data on government regulation of commercial aviation tariffs.
subfiles.summary: Original despatch is filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Japanese air carrier rates cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a Foreign Office note on regulation of Japanese air carrier rates.
subfiles.summary: Original despatch is filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Nagoya airport
subfiles.about: Records a report that construction of an airport at Nagoya would begin in 1933.
subfiles.summary: The reported completion date is 1938.
